bullet_text_verbatim: **Isolated sessions.** Each agent works in its own git worktree, so parallel sessions never fight over the same checkout.

**Any agent on your PATH.** Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, Copilot, Aider and others are detected automatically. Kolux launches them and bills through your own accounts; it bundles no models and no keys.
**One-click launch.** The `+` menu lists only the agents actually installed on the machine, so a new agent terminal is one click, or one keystroke once you bind a shortcut.
**Launch a shape, not a prompt.** Solo, Pair, Workbench and Swarm open several sessions at once and give each a distinct role, with a lineup you review before anything is created.
**Live status.** Managed hooks report whether each agent is working, waiting on you, or done.
**Automations.** Run a prompt on a schedule, hourly, daily or on a cron expression.
**Orchestration.** A first-class CLI creates runs and tasks, starts worker sessions from inside another agent, dispatches work between them, and carries messages in per-run mailboxes.
**Everything in one window.** Terminals, an editor, a browser and diff review sit side by side.
Everything you type, every file you open, and every agent's terminal output.
Repos, worktrees, settings, and saved credentials, all in your local profile folder.
**Update checks** — Kolux checks GitHub Releases for a newer version and downloads installers from there.
**The agent CLIs you run** (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini, etc.) talk to their own providers under their own accounts; Kolux does not proxy or log that traffic.
**The browser pane** loads whatever site you navigate it to, like any browser.
**Send Feedback / Report a crash** open a pre-filled GitHub issue in your browser for you to review and submit — Kolux does not send it for you.
Git, GitHub/GitLab/Bitbucket, and SSH actions you take go to the remotes and hosts you already configured.
